title: Kisumu-Style Caramelized Kenyan Halal Beef Tagine
description: A flavorful one-pot dish from Kisumu, Kenya, made with halal-friendly beef, leeks, and spices, all cooked to perfection in a traditional clay tajine.

ingredients.name: 1.5 lb beef brisket or beef shank, cut into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.notes: Halal-certified beef is a must for this recipe.

ingredients.name: 2 medium leeks, chopped (white and light green parts only)
ingredients.notes: Make sure to rinse the leeks thoroughly to remove any dirt.

ingredients.name: 2 cloves garlic, minced
ingredients.notes: Add more or less garlic to taste.

ingredients.name: 1 large onion, chopped
ingredients.notes: Use a sweet onion variety for the best flavor.

ingredients.name: 2 medium tomatoes, chopped
ingredients.notes: You can use fresh or canned tomatoes for this recipe.

ingredients.name: 2 tbsp olive oil
ingredients.notes: Use a neutral-tasting oil to prevent the flavors from overpowering the dish.

ingredients.name: 1 tsp ground cumin
ingredients.notes: You can adjust the amount of cumin to your liking.

ingredients.name: 1 tsp ground coriander
ingredients.notes: Use fresh coriander leaves as a garnish for added flavor and texture.

ingredients.name: 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
ingredients.notes: Cinnamon adds warmth and depth to the dish.

ingredients.name: 1/4 tsp ground cayenne pepper
ingredients.notes: Use more or less cayenne pepper depending on your desired level of heat.

ingredients.name: 1/2 cup beef broth
ingredients.notes: Use low-sodium broth or stock for a healthier option.

ingredients.name: 2 tbsp honey
ingredients.notes: You can adjust the amount of honey to your taste.

instructions: In a large clay tajine or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the chopped leeks and cook, stirring occasionally, until they start to brown and caramelize, about 10 minutes.
Add the beef and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cayenne pepper, and beef broth to the tajine. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the beef is tender and the sauce has thickened, about 1 1/2 hours.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and honey. Continue to simmer, uncovered, until the sauce has thickened and the flavors have melded together, about 10-15 minutes.
Season the tagine with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh coriander leaves and a dollop of yogurt, if desired.
Serve over couscous or rice, if desired.
